endorsements.quote: Encouraging the participation and input of a diverse range of stakeholders, including subject matter experts, community members, and representatives from marginalised groups, can help ensure that the impact of AI systems is thoroughly considered and that the perspectives of all affected stakeholders are taken into account.

unlisted_practices: Ensure AI systems are transparent and that their decision-making processes can be traced and audited to support accountability and trust.
Where transparency cannot be obtained, preserve and cultivate the competence to evaluate why an AI system reaches a given outcome and to assess value alignment.
Inform patients of the limitations of clinicians' understanding of the AI algorithm and its pros and cons so they can decide whether they prefer its use.
When AI-related medical errors occur, prioritize finding solutions and support for the victim over assigning blame.
Foster collaboration and partnerships among stakeholders so AI development and deployment are guided by shared responsibility and commitment to the common good.
Incorporate an Ubuntu-inspired collective forward-looking responsibility approach into AI ethical guidelines.

screen.reason: This is a philosophical conceptual paper/commentary proposing an Ubuntu-inspired ethical framework for addressing the responsibility gap in healthcare AI deployment.
